invariants_created: OPTIONS can be sent at any time, including before session establishment or during an active session
DESCRIBE typically precedes SETUP but is not strictly required by the protocol
SETUP must precede PLAY, PAUSE, and RECORD
PLAY can follow SETUP (READY→PLAYING) or PAUSE (READY→PLAYING after resume)
PAUSE can only be sent in PLAYING state, transitions to READY
TEARDOWN terminates the session and can be sent from any state (READY, PLAYING, RECORDING), transitioning to INIT
GET_PARAMETER can be sent at any time after session establishment (after SETUP)
DESCRIBE may fail with 404 and be retried; the session can continue after a successful DESCRIBE
The canonical lifecycle is OPTIONS → DESCRIBE → SETUP → PLAY → TEARDOWN
After TEARDOWN, the Session header is no longer valid and a new session must be established
RECORD transitions from READY to RECORDING state, requiring prior SETUP
REDIRECT is server-to-client only; client should teardown and reconnect to new URI
ALL.CSeq: Mandatory in every request and response. Must be a monotonically increasing integer. Client increments for each new request; server echoes the same CSeq in its response.
SETUP.Transport: Mandatory in SETUP request. Specifies transport protocol (RTP/AVP/UDP, RTP/AVP/TCP, etc.), client ports, server ports, interleaved mode, multicast/unicast, TTL, destination address.
PLAY.Session: Mandatory in PLAY request. Must be the session ID received from the SETUP response.
PAUSE.Session: Mandatory in PAUSE request. Must be the session ID received from the SETUP response.
TEARDOWN.Session: Mandatory in TEARDOWN request. Must be the session ID received from the SETUP response. After TEARDOWN, the session ID becomes invalid.
GET_PARAMETER.Session: Required after session establishment (post-SETUP). Optional before SETUP.
SET_PARAMETER.Session: Required after session establishment (post-SETUP).
RECORD.Session: Mandatory in RECORD request. Must be the session ID received from the SETUP response.
OPTIONS.Public: Response-only header. Lists comma-separated supported methods (e.g., 'OPTIONS, DESCRIBE, SETUP, PLAY, PAUSE, TEARDOWN, GET_PARAMETER').
DESCRIBE.Accept: Typically 'application/sdp' in request. Response Content-Type should match.
DESCRIBE.Content-Type: Response header, typically 'application/sdp' when body contains SDP.
PLAY.Range: Optional. Specifies playback range using NPT format (e.g., 'npt=0-', 'npt=10-20') or clock format (e.g., 'clock=20250101T120000Z-').
REDIRECT.Location: Mandatory in REDIRECT request. Specifies the new server URL to connect to.
ANNOUNCE.Content-Type: Must be 'application/sdp' when announcing session description.
ALL.Content-Length: Required if message body is present. Specifies byte length of body.

status_changes.description: INIT -> INIT via OPTIONS
status_changes.rationale: The heuristic trace augmentation directly shows this transition, and the invariant claim confirms OPTIONS can be sent at any time, including before session establishment.

status_changes.description: INIT -> DESCRIBED via DESCRIBE
status_changes.rationale: The heuristic trace augmentation directly shows this transition, consistent with the canonical lifecycle where DESCRIBE follows OPTIONS.

status_changes.description: DESCRIBED -> READY via SETUP
status_changes.rationale: The heuristic trace augmentation directly shows this transition, and the invariant confirms SETUP must precede PLAY/PAUSE/RECORD, establishing READY state.

status_changes.description: INIT -> READY via SETUP
status_changes.rationale: The heuristic trace augmentation shows this transition, but the canonical lifecycle suggests DESCRIBE typically precedes SETUP. While SETUP might be possible directly from INIT, the evidence is sparse and the protocol typically expects DESCRIBE first.

status_changes.description: READY -> PLAYING via PLAY
status_changes.rationale: The heuristic trace augmentation directly shows this transition, and the invariant confirms PLAY can follow SETUP (READY→PLAYING).

status_changes.description: PAUSED -> PLAYING via PLAY
status_changes.rationale: The heuristic trace shows PAUSED -> PLAYING via PLAY, but the invariant states PAUSE transitions PLAYING→READY, not PLAYING→PAUSED. The state naming is inconsistent - the invariant says PAUSE goes to READY, not PAUSED. This suggests a state naming mismatch in the trace augmentation.

status_changes.description: PLAYING -> PAUSED via PAUSE
status_changes.rationale: The heuristic trace shows PLAYING -> PAUSED via PAUSE, but the invariant states PAUSE transitions PLAYING→READY, not PLAYING→PAUSED. The state naming is inconsistent between the trace and the invariant claims.

status_changes.description: PLAYING -> CLOSED via TEARDOWN
status_changes.rationale: The heuristic trace augmentation directly shows this transition, and the invariant confirms TEARDOWN terminates the session from any state including PLAYING.

status_changes.description: READY -> CLOSED via TEARDOWN
status_changes.rationale: The heuristic trace augmentation directly shows this transition, and the invariant confirms TEARDOWN can be sent from READY state.

status_changes.description: RECORDING -> CLOSED via TEARDOWN
status_changes.rationale: The heuristic trace augmentation directly shows this transition, and the invariant confirms TEARDOWN terminates the session from any state including RECORDING.
